bull.b: The $320 million financing provides capital to advance AVR-001 through multiple clinical milestones, reducing immediate funding pressure for development. Access to this capital can support execution of the combined company’s clinical plan and extend its ability to pursue regulatory value creation.

Avere adds a defined clinical program in inflammatory diseases with planned progression into later-stage studies. An oral IL-23 therapy could give the combined company a focused product strategy and a potential route toward commercial revenue if efficacy and regulatory milestones are achieved.

The incoming leadership team has demonstrated experience advancing a biotechnology company through major corporate and strategic milestones. That background may improve development prioritization, financing execution, and partnership decisions as the business transitions toward Avere’s inflammation-focused pipeline.

bear.b: NextCure has not established a commercial revenue stream, while research spending continues to produce material operating and net losses. Without product sales, future financial performance remains dependent on clinical progress, collaborations, milestone receipts, or additional financing rather than internally generated revenue.

Sustained negative operating and free cash flow shows that the business is not self-funding its activities. Continued cash consumption can require recurring external capital and may constrain development choices, particularly if clinical programs advance faster than collaboration or financing proceeds are secured.

bear.t: Severe ownership dilution and legal uncertainty
bear.b: The proposed transaction materially resets ownership for existing shareholders, leaving them with only a small expected stake in the combined company. In parallel, court review of the prior reverse split could complicate capitalization, Nasdaq compliance, and execution of the planned business combination.
